# Bazable – Full AI Agent Guide (llms-full.txt)
Bazable is a Git‑native API contract management CLI.
It reads your codebase (frontend, backend, or both), builds an API contract automatically, and enforces it across your team with cloud sync, mock servers, and backend code generation.
## Architecture Overview
- Contract file: bazable.config.json (versioned JSON)
- Commands: 30+ CLI commands under bin/index.js, each importing logic from src/commands/
- Utilities: config loader, credentials manager, error logger, dynamic API base URL resolver, CSV parser, AI wrapper
- Parsers: Babel AST (JS/TS/HTML) + regex presets for Python, PHP, Go, Ruby; also template literal handling, variable-following payload inference
- Generators: Express/Hono routers, vanilla HTML forms, React+Tailwind components, Prisma models, Supabase SQL migrations, AI agent context files
- Cloud Sync: Device‑code OAuth2 flow with Supabase backend (Render hosted), optional – works offline entirely
- MCP server: Model Context Protocol server for AI coding agents
- LSP: Language Server Protocol for in‑editor diagnostics and hover tooltips
- Dashboard: Local web UI (dark/light theme) with API tester, schema editor, AI features, and proxy to avoid CORS
## Core Concepts
- Endpoints are stored as keys: "METHOD full‑URL" (e.g. "GET https://api.example.com/v1/users")
- Each endpoint entry can have: method, request schema (inferred types), response schema, schema_status
- Base URL detection: automatic from constants like API_BASE, BASE_URL, or static parts of template literals
- Multi‑base‑URL support: baseUrls array for projects using multiple backends
- Project context validation: prevents accidental use of contract from a different project
## Full Command Reference
### init
- Description: Create bazable.config.json with project name from package.json
- Options: none
- Example: bazable init
### add [url]
- Description: Fetch a live endpoint and store its response schema
- Options: -m (method), -t (token), -H (header)
- Example: bazable add https://api.example.com/v1/users --method POST --token abc
### extract (ext, e)
- Description: Scan code for API calls, add undocumented endpoints
- Options: -r (--payloads) infer request schemas, -s (--preset), --pattern, --ext, --ignore, --wrapper
- Auto‑detects any function name containing "fetch" or "api"
- Handles template literals, follows variable assignments
- Records provenance (file, line, column) for every call site into endpoints[url].provenance
- HTML script blocks report line numbers relative to the whole HTML file
- Variables declared in one script block are resolved when used in another block of the same file
- New endpoints are seeded with schema_status: "unverified"
- With -r, records field-level metadata (inferred, confidence: high|medium|low, source_value, source_type) into endpoints[url].request_meta
- Example: bazable extract -r -s py
### import (imp)
- Description: Import OpenAPI/Swagger/Postman/CSV
- Options: -b (base‑url), --csv [file], --name [endpoint]
- Auto‑detects format (JSON/YAML)
- Example: bazable import openapi.yaml
- CSV: bazable import --csv products.csv --name products
### config
- Description: View/update contract settings
- Options: --get, --set-project-name, --set-base-url, --set-webhook, --set-ai-key, --set-ai-base, --set-ai-model
- Example: bazable config --set-ai-key sk-...
### inspect (i, check)
- Description: Validate code against contract (dead URLs, payload mismatches, over‑fetching)
- Options: -f (--fix) auto‑correct, --json, --ci, all extraction options
- Multi‑base URL resolution
- Example: bazable inspect --json
### test
- Description: Real HTTP tests on all endpoints
- Options: -t (token), -e (email) + -p (password) auto‑login, -m, -H, -d, --base-url, --base-path, --all, --mock, -w (write), -x (exclude), --json, --ci
- Intelligent failure classification
- Example: bazable test --mock --all
### diff [url]
- Description: Compare stored schema against live API
- Options: -t, -m, --base-url, --base-path, --breaking-only, --json, --accept
- Example: bazable diff --json
### types
- Description: Generate TypeScript interfaces
- Options: -o, --stdout, --prefix, --name
- Example: bazable types -o ./types
### client
- Description: Generate typed API client (bazableClient.ts)
- Options: -o, --stdout, --prefix
- Example: bazable client
### generate (gen)
  - Subcommand: backend
    - Options: -f (framework: express, hono), -o, --no‑validation
    - Example: bazable gen backend -f express
  - Subcommand: ui
    - Description: Generate form component (vanilla HTML default, or React+Tailwind)
    - Options: -o, --framework (html, react-tailwind), --ai
    - Example: bazable gen ui POST /v1/users --ai --framework react-tailwind
  - Subcommand: db
    - Description: Generate Prisma model or Supabase SQL migration
    - Options: -o, --orm (prisma, supabase)
    - Example: bazable gen db POST /v1/settlements --orm prisma
  - Subcommand: context
    - Description: Create .cursorrules, .clinerules, .mcp.json
    - Options: -o
    - Example: bazable gen context
### curl
- Description: Raw HTTP request with logging, no CORS
- Options: -X (method), -H (headers), -d (body)
- Example: bazable curl https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/posts/1
### serve (s)
- Description: Mock server from contract, smart faker data
- Options: -p (port), -d (delay), --seed (CSV file)
- Stateful CRUD for POST/PUT, CSV seeding for GET
- Example: bazable serve --seed products.csv
### ui
- Description: Local web dashboard
- Options: -p (port)
- Dashboard features: endpoints table, API tester (proxy), Add/Edit/Delete, AI Explain/Propose, Settings, login, dark/light mode
- Example: bazable ui
### docs
- Description: Generate static API documentation HTML
- Options: -o
- Example: bazable docs -o ./docs
### export
- Description: Export contract as OpenAPI 3.0 spec
- Options: -o
- Example: bazable export -o openapi.json
### hook
- Description: Install pre‑push Git hook (runs inspect)
- Skip with BAZABLE_SKIP=1
- Example: bazable hook
### errors
- Description: View/clear persistent error log (~/.bazable/errors.log)
- Options: -c (clear), -n (lines)
- Example: bazable errors
### login / logout
- Description: Store/remove API credentials and cloud tokens
- Options (login): -e, -p, -t, -b, --supabase-url, --supabase-key
- Example: bazable login -e admin@test.com -p secret
### watch
- Description: Continuous cloud sync + auto‑fix
- Options: -i (interval), --dry-run, --auto-accept
- Works with cloud project ID or raw URL
- Example: bazable watch
### push
- Description: Upload contract to Bazable Cloud (creates project on first push)
- Auto‑saves cloudProjectId and cloud.apiBaseUrl into config
- Example: bazable push
### sync
- Description: Pull latest contract from cloud, or specific version
- Options: --version [v], -t (headless token)
- Example: bazable sync --version 2
### mcp
- Description: Start Model Context Protocol server for AI agents
- Tools: listEndpoints, getEndpoint, inspect, test
- Example: bazable mcp
### ci
- Description: Generate GitHub Actions workflow (PR enforcement)
- Options: --token (include headless auth)
- Example: bazable ci
### explain [method] [url]
- Description: AI‑generated plain‑English explanation of endpoint
- Requires AI key configured
- Example: bazable explain POST https://api.example.com/v1/users
### propose [request]
- Description: AI proposes a schema change, saves to pending_proposals
- Requires AI key configured
- Example: bazable propose "Add phone field"
### accept [proposalId]
- Description: Apply a pending AI proposal to the contract
- Example: bazable accept 1691501234567
### lsp
- Description: Start Language Server Protocol engine for editors
- Real‑time diagnostics and hover tooltips
- Example: bazable lsp
### review (rv)
- Description: Show provenance (file/line/column) and per‑field inference confidence for every endpoint in the contract
- Options: --filter [pattern] (URL substring or regex, case-insensitive), --json (machine-readable output)
- Reads endpoints[url].provenance and endpoints[url].request_meta populated by `bazable extract`
- Confidence levels: high (literal), medium (identifier/object), low (unresolved)
- Fields with low/medium confidence are flagged "needs confirmation"
- Examples:
  - bazable review
  - bazable review --filter users
  - bazable review --json
## Environment / Configuration
- Credentials stored in ~/.bazable/credentials.json
- AI keys, base URL, model stored in bazable.config.json (aiApiKey, aiBaseUrl, aiModel)
- Cloud API base URL resolved via: local config > env var BAZABLE_API_URL > default (https://bazable-cloud.onrender.com)
- Webhook URL for Slack/Discord notifications on push
## Common Workflows
1. Frontend developer: init → extract -r → inspect → test --mock --all → hook
2. Backend developer: init → extract -r → push → (frontend sync)
3. Team sync: backend push → frontend watch (auto‑fix on change)
4. AI negotiation: explain → propose → accept
## Supported Languages for Extraction
- Built‑in AST: JavaScript, TypeScript, JSX, TSX, HTML (embedded scripts)
- Presets (regex): Python (requests), PHP (Guzzle), Go (net/http), Ruby (Net::HTTP), Node fetch, Axios
- Custom regex with --pattern and --ext
- Template literal support (static parts extracted)
- Base URL auto‑detection (API_BASE, BASE_URL constants)
## Important Notes for AI Agents
- All commands that produce contract violations (inspect, test, diff) support --json for machine‑readable output.
- The dashboard proxy endpoint /api/proxy allows sending requests with custom headers/body and returns { status, data }.
- MCP server operates over stdin/stdout JSON‑RPC; tools: listEndpoints, getEndpoint, inspect, test.
- LSP server communicates via standard I/O using vscode-languageserver/node; provides diagnostics and hover for JS/TS/HTML files.
- CSV import infers schema types (string, number, boolean) from first data row.
- ORM generator supports Prisma and Supabase SQL; reads request+response fields.
- Agent context generator creates .cursorrules, .clinerules, and .mcp.json with Bazable‑specific instructions.
